name: Detail Loss Map
description: Generates spatial maps of detail loss to identify regions where AI generation produced unnatural smoothing.
mechanism:
This method creates pixel-level maps showing where fine image detail has been lost or suppressed, which is a hallmark of AI-generated and inpainted images:

1. **Multi-Scale Detail Extraction**: The image is decomposed into a Laplacian pyramid with 4–6 levels. At each scale, the detail coefficient energy (sum of squared Laplacian coefficients) is computed per 16×16 block. Natural photographs exhibit consistent detail energy ratios across scales following a power-law relationship with exponent α ≈ 0.7–1.0.

2. **Expected Detail Prediction**: A non-local means regression model predicts the expected detail energy at each location based on the local image content (edges, textures, flat regions). The model is trained on a dataset of authentic photographs and represents the expected detail-to-structure relationship for natural images.

3. **Anomaly Map Generation**: The detail loss map is computed as the ratio of observed to expected detail energy at each block. Values below 0.3 indicate significant detail suppression. The map is color-coded: green (normal detail, ratio 0.7–1.3), yellow (mild loss, 0.3–0.7), red (severe loss, < 0.3). AI-generated images typically show widespread yellow/red regions, especially in textured areas like hair, fabric, and foliage.

4. **Boundary Analysis**: At the boundaries between manipulated and authentic regions, detail energy often shows a sharp discontinuity. The method computes the gradient of the detail loss map and detects boundary pixels where the gradient magnitude exceeds 2σ of the map's gradient distribution, enabling precise segmentation of manipulated regions.
parameters:
Laplacian pyramid levels: 4–6
Block size: 16×16 pixels
Detail loss threshold: 0.3 (severe), 0.7 (mild)
Power-law exponent range: 0.7–1.0 for natural images
Boundary gradient threshold: 2σ
Minimum image size: 256×256 pixels
accuracy: 80–87% accuracy in detecting AI-generated images based on detail loss patterns. Boundary detection achieves F1-score of 0.78 for localization of manipulated regions. Performance is highest on AI images with noticeable smoothing (GAN-generated faces: 92%) and lower on high-quality diffusion model outputs (74%).
source: Wang, Z., Simoncelli, E. P., & Bovik, A. C. (2003). Multi-Scale Structural Similarity for Image Quality Assessment. IEEE Asilomar Conference on Signals, Systems and Computers.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated images by identifying unnatural smoothing patterns and detail suppression. Localizing inpainted or retouched regions where detail has been artificially removed. Quality assessment of image restoration algorithms by mapping detail preservation performance.
strengths:
• Provides intuitive visual output (color-coded detail loss maps)
• Effective at detecting the characteristic smoothing of GAN-generated images
• Multi-scale analysis captures detail loss at different spatial frequencies
• Boundary detection enables precise localization of manipulated regions
• Works well on faces, landscapes, and textured surfaces
limitations:
• Images with intentional blur (bokeh, motion blur) produce false positives in blurred regions
• Out-of-focus areas in authentic photos may be flagged as detail loss
• High-quality diffusion models (Stable Diffusion XL, Midjourney v5) produce less obvious detail loss
• Heavy JPEG compression causes genuine detail loss that can mask AI artifacts
• Requires training data (authentic photos) for the expected detail prediction model

references.title: Wang, Z., Simoncelli, E. P., & Bovik, A. C. — Multi-Scale Structural Similarity (MS-SSIM) (2003)
Zhu, X. & Milanfar, P. — Automatic Parameter Selection for Denoising Algorithms Using a No-Reference Measure of Image Content (2010)
Wang, S. Y. et al. — CNN-Generated Images Are Surprisingly Easy to Spot…for Now (CVPR 2020)
